extracted.intended_audience: conference organizers, program chairs, area chairs, reviewers, and OpenReview platform administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for running a large-scale double-blind conference peer-review process (NeurIPS 2021) on the OpenReview platform, including submission, reviewer recruitment/matching, reviewing, decisions, and post-decision publication policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review format and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Double blind, closed reviewing, with area chairs and senior area chairs, and meta-reviews, with the addition in 2021 of rolling reviewer discussion with authors (rather than a single author response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workflow was similar to prior years but added rolling reviewer discussion. Reviews are double-blind and closed during review; structure includes ACs, SACs and meta-reviews. Planning of workflow details and timing coordinated between PCs and OpenReview team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruiting scale and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Invited over 13k reviewers, 1k area chairs and 155 senior area chairs; with permission, shared list of accepted authors from prior conference years to help recruit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment may leverage past conference author lists; large-scale recruiting requires coordination and significant invitation volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent profiles and required registration
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview had ~228k researcher profiles; during reviewer recruiting and paper submission 11k profiles were created. NeurIPS required all authors (not just submitting authors) to register with OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiles incorporate papers from DBLP, author coreference, and verification by staff. Requiring author registration aids conflict-of-interest resolution and gathering multiple email addresses per person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest (COI) data collection and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Author and reviewer profiles include institution domain names, DBLP URL, Google Scholar URL, institutional history, advisors, collaborators, social connections, and other non-institutional conflicts; private conflicts can be recorded. For matching, conflicts were computed based on institution history, listed relations, and paper co-authorship within the last 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect extensive COI metadata and enable private conflicts. Use explicit rules (e.g., co-authorship within 3 years) and institutional history to compute conflicts programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Expertise models were built for all reviewers using OpenReview’s deep learning embedding methods run on titles and abstracts of reviewers’ papers. NeurIPS used only OpenReview’s expertise model instead of TPMS or Semantic Scholar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run automated embedding-based expertise extraction from reviewers' publications to produce affinities used in matching; choice of model can replace or augment other systems like TPMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and draft preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft paper titles and abstracts were submitted one week before the full-paper deadline. OpenReview received 11,729 paper submissions with many updates in the 24 hours before the final deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing early draft title/abstract submission can aid planning; expect heavy last-minute updates and design system capacity accordingly. Track and process submission updates (e.g., 42k updates observed).

rubrics_metrics.name: System capacity and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview multi-server system never surpassed 50% CPU usage during peaks, maintained smooth operation with rapid response; handled over 28k active users and >2.3k simultaneous users during the last hour of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for high concurrency and large traffic (thousands of simultaneous users), monitor server load, and ensure sub-second or rapid response times. System performance metrics (CPU, active users) matter for stability during deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding infrastructure and interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs bid on ACs and both ACs and reviewers bid on papers, assigned as a 'task' that was not complete until a given number of bids had been entered. Bidders could sort ACs/papers by affinity scores or search by metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support task-driven bidding with required counts, sorting by affinity, and metadata search to streamline bidding and ensure sufficient coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper–reviewer assignment methodology and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Affinities for matching included the expertise model, reviewer bids, and conflicts of interest. Optimization used Min-Cost-Flow and FairFlow; optimizer meta-parameters are tunable and chairs ran the optimizer many times (~60 minute turnaround). Each match comes with summary statistics about match quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-factor affinity scoring (expertise, bids, COIs) and advanced optimizers; provide tunable hyperparameters, quick re-run ability, and match-quality diagnostics. Allow browsing/editing of assignment results via UI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment browsing and manual edits
rubrics_metrics.description: The OpenReview 'Edge Browser' allowed PCs and ACs to browse match results, see reviewer loads and metadata, and make suggested edits to assignments, including inviting new reviewers not in the reviewing pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a rich UI for browsing matches (nested/column view), visibility into reviewer metadata and loads, and the ability to propose or make manual assignment changes and invite external reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-specific consoles and operational features
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized consoles were provided for reviewers, area chairs, senior area chairs, ethic reviewers, ethic chairs, and program chairs with task lists, reviewing status, filtering language, keyword search, reviewer re-assignment, aggregate statistics, status of bids, review completion status, email reminders, and CSV data dumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer role-tailored dashboards with filtering/query language, bulk operations (reminders, CSV exports), and status tracking to improve operational efficiency across roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review submission, visibility rules, and discussion organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews were entered directly, visible immediately to ACs, then visible to authors and reviewers of the same paper after the reviewing deadline. Multiple tabs were implemented in paper discussion (author discussion, committee discussion, all reviewing discussion, post-reviewing public discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and enforce visibility timing (e.g., AC visibility immediate, author visibility after deadline). Organize discussion into multiple, role-scoped threads/tabs to separate author interactions, committee deliberations, and public discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review counts and confidential comments handling
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview processed 37,284 reviews, 8,103 meta reviews, 452 ethics reviews, and 101,112 confidential comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support large volumes of reviews and confidential comments; provide mechanisms to store and manage confidential communication separate from public threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality rating and author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Area chairs were able to rate the quality of each review. Authors were allowed to provide review feedback. Ratings and feedback were only visible to the Program Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mechanisms for ACs and authors to rate and give feedback on reviews while restricting visibility of these ratings to program leadership to improve oversight and reviewer accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review configuration and process
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview added configuration to handle ethics reviews. Ethics Review Chairs assigned ethics reviewers to papers flagged with ethical issues, using the expertise matching system to suggest appropriate reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a separate configurable ethics-review pathway with assignment tools and expertise suggestions for ethically sensitive submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision finalization, editing, and publication workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview lets PCs download CSVs (including AC decisions), which PCs edited in Google Sheets; some decisions were modified, then OpenReview emailed and posted the decisions based on the Google Sheet. Future options include in-UI editing or tighter Google Sheets integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable CSV export/import and external editing (e.g., Google Sheets) for decision workflows, but consider tighter UI integration or bi-directional syncing to reduce external tooling dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready and post-accept requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview created upload invitations and tasks for accepted-paper authors for copyright form, supplementary materials (including videos), and camera-ready LaTeX zip file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured post-accept tasks and upload slots to collect required forms and supplementary artifacts in a standardized way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper clustering and track formation using affinity scores
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview provided affinity scores between accepted papers as input to paper clustering for conference track assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute inter-paper affinity metrics to assist in clustering accepted papers into tracks or sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public release and opt-in policy for rejected papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers were made public and open for non-anonymous public commenting along with their anonymous reviews, meta-reviews, and author responses. Rejected submissions were by default not made public, but authors of rejected submissions were given 2 weeks to opt in to make their de-anonymized papers public and open for commenting; if they opted in this also opened up reviews and discussions. About 2% of rejected papers opted in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a policy that automatically publishes accepted papers with review artifacts, and implement an opt-in window for rejected papers to be de-anonymized and opened for public comment to allow transparency while respecting authors' choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission declaration and randomized visibility experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were asked to declare if a previous version had been rejected elsewhere and to describe improvements made. Resubmission information was made visible to reviewers and area chairs for a randomly chosen 50% of submissions to evaluate resubmission bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect resubmission history and descriptions of improvements at submission time and consider randomized visibility of this data to measure and mitigate resubmission bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision consistency experiment (noise audit)
rubrics_metrics.description: A consistency experiment was run where a variant of the 2014 NeurIPS experiment was repeated (10% of submissions reviewed by two independent program committees) to quantify randomness in decisions; results reported separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run controlled split-review experiments to quantify decision consistency across program committees and assess the impact of scale on review variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author perception survey experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview implemented a two-part author survey to understand how well authors’ perception of their submissions agrees with reviewing outcomes; results forthcoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use author surveys to measure perceived fairness and alignment between author expectations and review outcomes; treat results as input for process improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform support level and customization
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview technical staff provided 24/7 support to NeurIPS program chairs, including rapid responses and custom work. OpenReview is a flexible platform allowing heavy customization and support for experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure vendor/platform support for large conferences includes around-the-clock assistance and the ability to implement custom features and experiments requested by program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned feature improvements to support workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned improvements included redesigning the paper reviewing discussion forum, further improvements to reviewer-paper matching, a new API for finer-grained control of visibility and history, CRON-jobs for automated reminders, synchronous chat-style communication among reviewers/ACs/PCs, and support for live conferences integrated into the reviewing platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize features that address rolling discussions, fine-grained visibility control, historical change tracking, automated operational jobs, and synchronous communication to enhance interactivity and operational efficiency.
